On the Regularization Landscape for the Linear Recommendation Models

Dong Li1  Zhenming Liu2  Ruoming Jin1  Hao Zhou1  Zhi Liu3  Jing Gao3  Bin Ren2 1 Kent State University, USA 2 College of William and Mary, USA 3 iLambda, USA {dli12,rjin1,hzhou6}@kent.edu {zliu,jgao}@ilambda.com {zliu,bren}@cs.wm.edu
Abstract

Recently, a wide range of recommendation algorithms inspired by deep learning techniques have emerged as the performance leaders on several standard recommendation benchmarks. While these algorithms were built on different DL techniques (e.g., dropouts, autoencoder), they have similar performance and even similar cost functions. This paper studies whether the models’ comparable performance are sheer coincidence, or they can be unified under a single framework. We find that all linear performance leaders effectively add only a nuclear-norm based regularizer, or a Frobenius-norm based regularizer. The former ones possess a (surprising) rigid structure that limits the models’ predictive power but their solutions are low rank and have closed form. The latter ones are more expressive and more efficient for recommendation but their solutions are either full-rank or require executing hard-to-tune numeric procedures such as ADMM. Along this line of finding, we further propose two low-rank, closed-form solutions, derived from carefully generalizing Frobenius-norm based regularizers. The new solutions get the best of both nuclear-norm and Frobenius-norm world.

1 Introduction

Research progress on algorithms for recommendation has escalated in recent years, partially fueled by the adoption of deep learning techniques. However, recent studies have found that many new deep learning recommendation models have shown sub-par performance against the simpler linear recommendation models (Dacrema et al., 2019a; Rendle et al., 2019). Although some studies are available to analyze linear vs non-linear models (Dacrema et al., 2019a), it remains puzzling why these seemingly different techniques all result in models with similar performance or even similar cost functions. This motivates us to ask a fundamental question:

What is the barebones engine that drives the performance improvement for the recent recommendation algorithms?

Specifically, do different recommendation techniques offer different “magic”, but coincidentally have similar performance, or can they be unified under a single framework, which has a potential to produce one single algorithm that gets the best of all existing works? In the latest study, Jin et al. (2021) examines the relationship between the widely used matrix factorization (MF), such as ALS (Warlop et al., 2017), and the linear autoencoders (LAE) which encompasses the recent performance leaders, such as EASE (Steck, 2019) and EDLAE (Steck, 2020). They consider two basic regularization forms (See Eq (1) and (6)) and found that the optimal (closed-form) solutions of both models recover the direction of principal components, while shrinking the corresponding singular values differently. They suggests this difference may enable LAE to utilize a larger number of latent dimensions to improve recommendation accuracy, and use this to highlight the similarity as well as difference between LAE and MF.

In this paper, we go much beyond the two basic models studied in  Jin et al. (2021) to analyze a large number of recent performance leaders of (linear) recommender algorithms. We found they all can be categorized into those that implement nuclear-norm regularizers, and into those that implement Frobenius-norm regularizers. We found that the former ones possess a (surprising) rigid structure that limits the models’ predictive power, and the latter ones tend to be more expressive and more effective for recommendation. In many cases, both regularizers recover the direction of principal components, while shrinking the corresponding singular values differently. Interestingly, we observe that it is not matrix factorization or LAE that determines the shrinkage structure (as  Jin et al. (2021) suggested), but instead it is the forms of regularization. Thus, this paper provides a more complete and accurate characterization on how a linear recommendation model performs under different regularizations.

To better understand the regularizations that can be transformed into the (weighted) nuclear-norm regularizer ‖W‖∗\|W\|_{*}, we first show that Variational Linear AutoEncoders (VLAE) solves a weighted nuclear-norm regularization problem, in which the weights possess a specific combinatorial structure. We also show that this technique cannot be generalized to tackle arbitrary weight sequences. Second, it has been known that using dropout techniques is equivalent to adding a squared nuclear-norm regularizer ‖W‖∗2\|W\|^{2}_{*}, and that the solution structure is strikingly similar to the regularizer that uses ‖W‖∗\|W\|_{*}. we generalize the result to show that the solution structures for ‖W‖∗p\|W\|^{p}_{*} are highly similar for all p≥1p\geq 1. But when p=1,2p=1,2, the solution and hyper-parameters possess favorable properties so hyper-parameter search becomes easier. This also partially explains why only p=1,2p=1,2 have been extensively considered. Third, all nuclear-norm–based techniques possess a salient property: their estimators keep the singular vectors of the data matrix and shrink only the singular values. But this severely limits the search space and explains why models that use only nuclear-norm–based regularizers share the same performance ceiling even when hyper-parameters are extensively searched.

The (weighted) Frobenius-norm regularizers ‖Λ​W‖F2\|\Lambda W\|^{2}_{F} are implemented in EASE (Steck, 2019) and EDLAE (Steck, 2020). These models produce closed form full-rank estimators; and if the zero diagonal constraint on WW is enforced, their singular vectors will no longer coincide with those of the data, and can deliver (slightly) better performance. However, no closed form solutions for the low-rank estimator is known and the current approaches rely on ADMM or stochastic factorized gradients (Steck, 2020). In this paper, we propose two new low-rank, closed-form estimators that deliver comparable results to the full rank models (EASE and full-rank EDLAE) as well as the ADMM based solutions (Steck, 2020).

The new closed-form solutions for low-rank models have profound implications at both practical and conceptual fronts: First, low rank solutions are often more scalable (the full rank WW can be too large to materialize) and can better serve real-world training and deployment. Second, perhaps more excitingly, these solutions get the best of nuclear (closed form and low rank) and Frobenius worlds (strong predictive power). A simple “one-liner” formula (from each solution) concisely pack all the benefits obtained by a recent long line of research and abstract out all the computation nuance (e.g., the need to tune ADMM and deal with local optimal). We believe these closed-form solutions are also powerful tools to help us compare different regularizations analytically.

2 Background and overview

Recommendation system background. Recommendation algorithms can be categorized into explicit ones that aim to predict unseen ratings between a user and an item and implicit ones that aim to predict actions, such as user click or add-cart (Steck, 2019; Dacrema et al., 2019b; Zhang et al., 2019). We focus on the implicit problem because it is more economically relevant. Here, let nn be the number of items and mm be the number of users. We are given a binary matrix X∈{0,1}m×nX\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n} that represents the interaction between users and items so far, i.e., Xi,j=1X_{i,j}=1 iff user ii has purchased or made a rating on item jj. Our goal is to produce a real-valued matrix X^\hat{X}, which we evaluate against future interactions using information retrieval metrics such as Top-kk or nDCG. Note that while the syntax of this problem resembles matrix completion (MC) (Candès and Tao, 2010)，推荐系统和MC有不同的评估标准，因此MC的结果不能直接适用于此。, recommendation systems and MC have different evaluation criteria so MC’s results are not directly applicable here.

5 实验结果Experimental Results

在本节中，我们通过实验研究线性推荐模型的不同正则化。 我们的目标是验证各种正则化（所有正则化都可以分类为核范数和弗罗贝尼乌斯范数）及其简单的封闭式解决方案的有效性。 我们旨在回答三个问题：In this section, we experimentally study different regularizations for linear recommendation models. Our goal is to validate the effectiveness of various regularizations (all can be categorized under nuclear norm and Frobenius norm) together with their simple closed-form solutions. We aim to answer three questions:Q1.与 ADMM 解决方案（第 4 节）相比，低秩 Frobenius 范数的封闭形式解的表现如何，以及用于矩阵分解的加权核范数正则化器如何表现（命题How does the closed form solution of low rank Frobenius norm perform compared with the ADMM solutions (Section 4) and how does the weighted nuclear norm regularizer for matrix factorization (Proposition2和推论and Corollary1）执行？) perform?Q2。Q2.因素数量（排名What is the tradeoff between the number of factors (rankkk）和推荐准确率？) and the recommendation accuracy?Q3。Q3.如何将权重从小到大（非降序）排序来调整奇异值（推论How does the ordering of weights from small to large (non-descending) for adjusting the singular values (Corollary1）影响推荐性能？) affect the recommendation performance?

6 结论与讨论Conclusion and Discussion

这项工作对最近提出的推荐系统线性模型进行了完整的分析。尽管这些模型利用了不同的深度学习技术，但它们实现了相似的性能。我们发现这并不巧合：所有模型都添加了基于核范数的（引理This work provides a complete analysis on the recently proposed linear models for recommendation systems. Despite that models leverage different deep learning techniques, they achieve similar performance. We find that this is not coincident: all the models add either a nuclear-norm-based (Lemma1）或基于 Frobenius 范数的正则化器。基于核范数的方法导致估计量保持) or a Frobenius-norm based regularizer. The nuclear-norm-based approach results in estimators that keepXX的奇异向量并以相当严格的方式缩小其奇异值（命题’s singular vectors and shrink its singular values in a quite rigid way (Proposition2和引理and Lemma2），这限制了他们的预测能力。 Frobenius 范数模型更加表达（命题), which limit their prediction power. The Frobenius-norm models are more express (Proposition1）且有效，但它们的估计器要么是满秩的，要么没有封闭式解。为了充分利用核世界和弗罗贝尼乌斯世界， 我们提出了两个低秩和封闭式估计器（第 2 节）。) and effective but their estimators are either full-rank or do not have closed form solutions. To get the best of both nuclear and Frobenius worlds, we propose two low-rank and closed-form estimators (Sec.4）基于仔细概括基于 Frobenius 范数的正则化器。这些估计器具有与线性性能领先者相比的竞争性能，因此简洁地打包了最近一系列研究所获得的所有好处，并抽象出了所有计算的细微差别。) based on carefully generalizing Frobenius-norm based regularizers. These estimators have competitive performance against linear performance leaders, and thus concisely pack all the benefits obtained by a recent long line of research and abstract out all the computation nuance.

推荐方面已有广泛的研究There have been extensive researches on recommendation[Aggarwal, 2016]。除了基本的基于用户和基于项目的协同过滤. Besides the basic user-based and item-based collaborative filtering[Deshpande and Karypis, 2004]，满秩线性自动编码器方法包括 SLIM, the full rank linear autoencoder approaches include SLIM[Ning and Karypis, 2011], 整体主义, HOLISM[Christakopoulou and Karypis, 2014], 轻松, EASE[Steck, 2019], DLAE（去噪线性自动编码器）, DLAE (Denoising linear autoencoder)Steck [2020]，而低秩方法包括, whereas low-rank approaches include[Kabbur et al., 2013, Sedhain et al., 2016, Steck, 2020]。为了泛化目的，所有定制的推荐都强制执行零对角线约束，而我们展示了没有零对角线约束的两项吉洪诺夫正则化的近似封闭式解决方案，可以与这些模型一样有效。. All the customized recommendation has been enforcing zero diagonal constraints for generalization purpose, whereas we show an approximate closed-form solution for a two-term Tikhonov regularization without the zero diagonal constraint can be as effective as these models.

矩阵分解在实践中得到了广泛的研究，部分原因是 Netflix 的竞争Matrix factorization has been been widely studied in practice, partially due to Netflix competitionKoren et al. [2009]。 SVD++ 等方法. Methods like SVD++Koren [2008]和隐式交替最小二乘法 (ALS)and implicit Alternating Least Square (ALS) methodHu et al. [2008]（也称为加权矩阵分解）非常有影响力。(also weighted matrix factorization) have been very influential.[Jin et al., 2021]显示了线性自动编码器和矩阵分解之间的关系，并指出了线性自动编码器的潜在优势。在这项工作中，我们进一步揭示了吉洪诺夫正则化线性自动编码器与包括矩阵分解在内的其他一些正则化之间的更深层次关系，并展示了正则化类别的潜在局限性。 我们还利用线性变分自动编码器（LVAE）来研究基于深度 VAE 的推荐方法shows the relationship between linear autoencoders and matrix factorization, and pointed out a potential advantage of linear autoencoders. In this work, we take a step further to reveal a deeper relationship between Tikhonov regularized linear autoencoders and a few other regularizations including matrix factorization, and show the potential limitation of the class of regularization. We also utilize the linear variational autoencoders (LVAE) to study how the deep VAE based recommendation approaches[Li and She, 2017, Liang et al., 2018, Shenbin et al., 2020]与线性自动编码器和矩阵分解有关。relate to linear autoencoders and matrix factorization.

外部推荐，最近有一些关于线性（变分）自动编码器的正则化景观的研究Outside recommendation, there have been a few recent studies on regularization landscapes of linear (variational) autoencoders[Kunin et al., 2019, Bao et al., 2020, Lucas et al., 2019a]。他们不提供一般加权. They do not provide the general weightedℓ2\ell_{2}正则化，因此没有发现正则化（对于 MF）的固有限制。我们的 LVAE 启发正则化之前也从未被研究过。regularization and thus did not find the inherent limitation on the regularization (for MF). Our LVAE inspired regularization is also never studied before.

核范数正则化器可以在向量回归设置中恢复低秩矩阵Nuclear norm regularizers can recover low-rank matrices in the vector regression setting[Negahban and Wainwright, 2011]。其加权泛化可应用于图像处理领域. Its weighted generalization can be applied in the area of image processing[Gu et al., 2014]。由于加权核范数通常不是凸的或可微的，因此除了少数特殊情况外，找到最优解很困难. Because weighted nuclear-norm is usually not convex or differentiable, finding optimal solutions is difficult except for a few special cases[Chen et al., 2013].

C.2 带有 Dropout 超参数调整的矩阵分解Matrix Factorization with Dropout Hyperparameters Tuning

Cavazza et al. [2018]表明使用 dropout 进行优化（允许排名优化）等价于用核范数求解矩阵逼近问题：shows that optimization with dropout (allowing rank optimizing) is equivalent to solving a matrix approximation problem with nuclear norm:

minP,Q,d⁡‖X−P​QT‖F2+d​1−pp⋅∑k=1d‖Pk‖22⋅‖Qk‖22minY⁡‖X−Y‖F2+1−pp​‖Y‖∗2\begin{split}&\min_{P,Q,d}{||X-PQ^{T}||^{2}_{F}+d\frac{1-p}{p}\cdot\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d}||P_{k}||^{2}_{2}\cdot||Q_{k}||^{2}_{2}}\\ &\min_{Y}{||X-Y||^{2}_{F}}+\frac{1-p}{p}||Y||^{2}_{*}\\ \end{split}

解由下式给出：and the solution is given by:

X=SVDU​Σ​VTY∗=P∗⋅(Q∗)T=U⋅Sμ​(Σ)⋅VTSμ​(σ)=max⁡(σ−μ,0)μ=1−pp+(1−p)​d¯​∑i=1d¯σi​(X)\begin{split}X&\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{SVD}}}{{=}}U\Sigma V^{T}\\ Y^{*}&=P^{*}\cdot(Q^{*})^{T}\\ &=U\cdot S_{\mu}(\Sigma)\cdot V^{T}\\ S_{\mu}(\sigma)&=\max(\sigma-\mu,0)\\ \mu&=\frac{1-p}{p+(1-p)\bar{d}}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{\bar{d}}{\sigma_{i}(X)}\end{split}

哪里whered¯\bar{d}表示满足以下条件的最大整数：denotes the largest integer such that:

σd¯​(X)>1−pp+(1−p)​d¯​∑i=1d¯σi​(X)\sigma_{\bar{d}}(X)>\frac{1-p}{p+(1-p)\bar{d}}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{\bar{d}}{\sigma_{i}(X)}

因此，只有一个参数Hence, there is only one parameterpp来调整。我们在下面的验证集上展示了调整过程，请参阅to tuning. We present the tuning process on the validation set below, seetables 9, 9和and9。最佳参数以及诱导排名. Optimal parameters as well as induced rankd¯\bar{d}被突出显示。are highlighted.

C.3 资源Resources

我们的代码主要在 CUDA 11.0 上的 Numpy 1.19、Pytorch 1.7.1 中实现。我们的实验在具有两个插槽的节点上进行，每个插槽包含 24 核 Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8268 CPU @ 2.90GHz 和 4 个 GeForce RTX 3090 24GB 显存 GPU。Our code are mainly implemented in Numpy 1.19, Pytorch 1.7.1 on CUDA 11.0. Our experiments are performed on nodes with two sockets, each containing a 24-core Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8268 CPU @ 2.90GHz and 4 GeForce RTX 3090 24GB memory GPU.
